sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: This bulbous lily grows in thickets and grassy slopes of north-east China, Korea and the Russian Far East. Its stem can reach about 65 cm; the bulb is 2.5–4 cm across.

sections.title: Leaves and flowers
sections.text: The narrow leaves are about 8–12 cm long and 2–4 mm wide. A stem bears one to six pendent, spotted pink-purple flowers, with strongly recurved tepals 3.5–4.5 cm long. The capsule is about 1.2–2 cm long.

sections.title: Caution
sections.text: No food use of the bulb was verified for this species. True lilies (Lilium) can cause severe kidney poisoning in cats; keep every part of the plant away from cats.

sources.title: Veterinary toxicology review — lilies and cats
